theory.intro: A diagonal of a quadrilateral joins two vertices that are not next to each other. As well as its side and angle properties, each special quadrilateral has diagonal properties that are always true, and the marks on a figure show which of them hold. **Bisect** means to cut into two equal parts.
facts: The diagonals **bisect each other** in a parallelogram, a rhombus, a rectangle and a square.
The diagonals are **equal in length** in a rectangle and a square only.
The diagonals **cross at right angles** in a rhombus, a square and a kite.
The diagonals **bisect the angles at the vertices** in a rhombus and a square.
In a **kite** the axis diagonal bisects the other diagonal at right angles, but it is not bisected itself.
A **trapezium** has none of these diagonal properties.
steps: Name the quadrilateral from its side and angle marks.
Read its diagonals: are they equal, do they cross at right angles, and does each cut the other in half?
State the property in full, saying which parts are equal or which angle is a right angle.

foundation.solution_text:
The two halves of one diagonal carry matching single ticks, and the two halves of the other carry matching double ticks.
Each diagonal is cut into two equal parts, so the diagonals bisect each other.

All four halves carry the same single tick, so every half is the same length.
The two diagonals are equal in length, and each one bisects the other.

The small square sits at the point where the two diagonals cross.
The diagonals cross at right angles.

The short diagonal is split into two equal parts, and the crossing is marked as a right angle.
The long diagonal bisects the short diagonal at right angles, but the short diagonal does not bisect the long one.

foundation.question_text: Are the diagonals of a parallelogram always equal in length?
foundation.solution_text:
The diagonals of a parallelogram always bisect each other, but one is usually longer than the other.
No — among the parallelograms, only a rectangle and a square have equal diagonals.

foundation.question_text: Do the diagonals of a rhombus always bisect the angles at its vertices?
foundation.solution_text:
Each diagonal of a rhombus runs from one vertex to the opposite vertex and splits both of those angles into two equal parts.
Yes.

foundation.question_text: State what is always true about the opposite angles of a parallelogram.
foundation.solution_text:
The angles at opposite corners of a parallelogram are the same size.
Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal.

foundation.question_text: State what is always true about the angles of a kite.
foundation.solution_text:
The two angles where a short side meets a long side are the same size.
One pair of opposite angles of a kite is equal.

foundation.question_text: The diagonals of a quadrilateral are equal in length, they bisect each other, and they cross at right angles. Name the quadrilateral.
foundation.solution_text:
Only one special quadrilateral has all three diagonal properties at once.
Square

development.question_text: Which diagonal property does every rectangle have that a parallelogram need not have?
development.solution_text:
The diagonals of both shapes bisect each other.
Only in the rectangle must the two diagonals also be equal in length.

development.question_text: Which diagonal property does every rhombus have that a rectangle need not have?
development.solution_text:
The diagonals of both shapes bisect each other.
Only in the rhombus must the two diagonals also cross at right angles.

development.question_text: Do the diagonals of a trapezium bisect each other? Explain your answer.
development.solution_text:
A trapezium has only one pair of parallel sides, so there is nothing forcing the crossing point to the middle of either diagonal.
No — a trapezium has none of the special diagonal properties.

development.question_text: The diagonals of a quadrilateral bisect each other and cross at right angles, but they are not equal in length. Name the quadrilateral.
development.solution_text:
Diagonals that bisect each other at right angles belong to a rhombus or a square.
Unequal diagonals rule out the square.
Rhombus

mastery.question_text: The diagonals of a quadrilateral bisect each other and are equal in length, but they do not cross at right angles. Name the quadrilateral, and state what would also have to be true of its diagonals for it to be a square.
mastery.solution_text:
Diagonals that bisect each other and are equal belong to a rectangle.
Rectangle
For a square, the diagonals would also have to cross at right angles.

mastery.question_text: Sam says that if the diagonals of a quadrilateral bisect each other then the quadrilateral must be a rectangle. Name a quadrilateral that shows Sam is wrong, and state the extra diagonal property a rectangle has.
mastery.solution_text:
The diagonals of every parallelogram bisect each other, and a parallelogram need not have any right angles.
A parallelogram that is not a rectangle shows Sam is wrong.
The extra property of a rectangle is that its two diagonals are also equal in length.
